findings.title: test_dedupe in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue has mismatched group_keys, will fail
findings.body: The test builds the expected `occurrence` and `event_data` with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, so the occurrence's fingerprint is `[f"{handler.detector.id}:val1"]` (via `handler.build_fingerprint("val1")`). However, the test then constructs `expected_result = DetectorEvaluationResult("group_key", ...)` and passes `expected_result.group_key` (i.e. `"group_key"`) into `handler.evaluate_group_key_value(...)`. Internally that calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data("group_key", 10, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` -> `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "group_key", 10, ...)` producing an occurrence whose fingerprint is `[f"{handler.detector.id}:group_key"]`. Since IssueOccurrence is a dataclass with field-by-field `__eq__`, the fingerprints differ and the assertion `... == expected_result` will fail. The expected occurrence must be built with the same group_key passed into `evaluate_group_key_value`.

findings.title: Inconsistent value passed to build_mock_occurrence_and_event in multiple tests
findings.body: Several tests pass `value=6` to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` even though the data packet being evaluated contains different values. For example: `test_state_results_multi_group` calls `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` while the data packet has `group_vals: {"group_2": 10}`; `test_results_on_change` calls it with `value=6` while the packet has `val1: 100`; `test_dedupe` calls it with `value=6` while the packet has `val1: 8`; `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` calls it with `value=6` while `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with `value=10`. Currently the value isn't used inside `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` so the tests pass, but the inconsistency obscures intent and any future change that incorporates `value` into the occurrence or event_data will silently produce wrong assertions.

findings.title: dedupe_update is enqueued before condition_group is validated
findings.body: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, `self.enqueue_dedupe_update(group_key, dedupe_value)` is called immediately after the dedupe check and BEFORE the `if not self.condition_group: ... return None` early return. As a result, data packets routed to detectors that have no valid condition group are still recorded as 'processed' in Redis (the dedupe value is bumped in `commit_state_updates`). If the condition group is later attached, those prior packets will be skipped even though no evaluation actually ran for them, causing potentially missed detections. The enqueue should be moved after the condition_group check, or only enqueued on the paths that perform real evaluation.

findings.title: Kafka produce exceptions prevent state commit, causing duplicate detections
findings.body: `process_detectors` calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` (which calls `produce_occurrence_to_kafka`) BEFORE `handler.commit_state_updates()`. If Kafka is unavailable or `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` raises, the exception propagates out of the loop and `commit_state_updates()` is never executed for that detector. The Redis dedupe value is therefore not updated, so on the next processing of the same data packet the detector will re-emit the same occurrence (and re-trigger downstream workflows). This is also exposed more by the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` path which can now raise from subclass code and have the same effect. Either wrap the produce in a try/except or commit dedupe state after successful produces.

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now extends StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing required abstract methods
findings.body: The PR changes `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` from `DetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` to `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]`, but the body remains `pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and now also the newly-added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Instantiating `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` (or any code path that constructs this handler) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ... with abstract methods ...`. Since `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is wired up in the same file, this will break the moment anyone references `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler`. Either leave `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` extending the non-abstract `DetectorHandler`, or implement the abstract methods (or at minimum add `detector_handler = None` until the abstraction is built).
